changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`

- names `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Both marketplace chunks were held by CHUNK CO-TENANCY, not by any import of the page: rolldown had parked `components/SuggestedBindingsPanel.tsx` (statically imported by the eager `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) in the first, and `console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx` (bare-imported by the package barrel for its SDUI registration) in the second. An `app-shell-eager-leaves` group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` isolates those co-tenants so the three declared-lazy pages chunk by their own dynamic-only reachability. The console eager closure moves 3180.2 KB → 3171.5 KB gzipped (−8,888 bytes, 48 → 45 eager chunks) with the three per-chunk ceilings unmoved.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `dded788ad` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1818 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2428 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36738980450)

PR objectui#11230 for card objectui#11204 (p1; triage `5911686087`, unlock `5913035564`, claim `5913109805`, dev report `5914734135`). Inputs: the card body and its four comments, the PR body, its three-file list, the net diff against `main` at the head, the head source read through the contents API, and the head's check-runs with `filter=latest` (42 at the first read, 43 at completion).

### ① Derived judgments

**Check-runs on the head.** Read at the start with ten runs still in progress, then re-read until every run had completed (the last, the `Test` aggregate, landed before the wait cap). 43 runs: 40 success, 3 skipped (the two coverage jobs and dependabot, skipped by design), 0 failure, none still running. Green: the eight `Test` shards and their `Test` aggregate, which carry the new pin file and objectui#11202's unmodified suite; Type Check; Lint; Build & E2E; Test (dist pins); Spec Main Shape Gate; Governed Surface Queue Guard; Line Citation Gate; Control Byte Scan; the five changeset gates; Bundle Analysis; and the docs and skill checks. These conclusions are the gate verdicts this record rests on.

**The base measurements (right).** Six cases, 5 red / 1 green on base `c3df43a42`, taken in a detached base worktree with the new pin file copied in. The five red are the readings the report and the PR table state: Automations 'Kick-off' sent with 'Kick-off two' on screen; Data autosave three fields sent with '4 fields' shown; Data reorder two fields sent with '3 fields' shown; the page inspector 'Welcome' sent with 'Welcome two' in the input; the nav with `navGen`, one save equal to the buffer yet dirty for good, "Done" unable to close. The one green is the Data control (a reorder with nothing edited meanwhile is the only save), which is base behaviour and has to be green there. The Automations row is objectui#11189's reading reproduced, so the control the direction asked for is in place; Data and the page inspector were measured before the fix, as the direction required, and both reproduce. Right.

**The `DraftSend` claim (right, with notes).** At the head `useDraftAutoSave` (`:217`, not exported) hands every send a claim whose `unmoved()` is an equality between `pendingRef.current.snapKey` and the serialised key it sent, and each caller's post-await clear runs only while that holds.
- Content, where the direction said "snapshot or generation": inside the direction, and the better of the two. A generation cannot tell an edit undone during the flight from one that was not: on A→B→A the generation leaves dirty set, and because `lastAttemptRef` already holds A's key the timer never sends A again, so dirty is stuck for good, with the leave guard and "Done" held. That is the nav row on base. Content reads A→B→A as unmoved, which is the truth (the server holds A), and clears. Right.
- Cost: `unmoved()` is a string equality on `snapKey`, which the hook already memoises per snapshot change, so a check serialises nothing; `sending(body)` serialises once per self-sent save. Cheap. Right.
- A key-order or undefined-only difference reads as moved and costs one extra save that then lands unmoved. Harmless.
- Pre-existing, not widened, no finding: an edit that brings the buffer back to the last attempted key inside the debounce (B sent and landed, then B→C→B) leaves dirty set with nothing sent, on base and on the head alike, because `lastAttemptRef` refuses a repeat. A limitation of the objectui#5813 / objectui#11189 dedupe, not of this PR; the seat may file it.

**Every post-await clear goes through the claim (right).** Nine `set*Dirty(false)` sites at the head. Five are save completions and all five read the claim: page inspector `doSave` `:2131`, nav `doNavSave` `:2175`, Data `doSave` `:3329`, Data `doReorderFields` `:3376`, Automations `doSave` `:4251`. The four unconditional ones are buffer replacements, as the report says: `:1722` the nav read-only put-back (`setAppDraft(navBaselineRef.current)`, then the clear); `:2102` the page load after `setDraft(body ?? baseline)`; `:3148` the Data load, synchronous, before its await; `:4225` the Automations load's `finally`. Each verified; none completes a save.

**`navGen` folded (right).** Zero references to `navGen`, `setNavGen`, `sentGen` or a `.gen` member remain at the head. The state, its bump in `onNavPatch` and the committed generation are gone; `navCommittedRef` keeps `dirty` alone, and its one reader, the same-package install guard at `:1971`, is unchanged. The nav autosave can use the hook's mechanism because its snapshot is `appDraft` and every `onNavPatch` writes `appDraft`; `doNavSave` sends a cleaned copy of exactly that snapshot, and the claim is on the buffer, which is the right subject (the question is whether the buffer moved, not whether the body differs). The report says which: content, not a count. objectui#11202's test file is not in this PR's file list, so its pins are unmodified; their colour on the head is the Test shards' verdict, below.

**The hook's return and the layout effect (right; no risk found).** `flush` keeps its behaviour and its identity (a state initialiser); its only reader is the nav "Done" effect at `:2196`, which lists it as a dependency. `sending` is new and module-private. `pendingRef` and `saveRef` are now written in a layout effect: refs only, no setState and no DOM work, so no render cascade; a layout effect is current before any passive effect of the same commit, and both readers (`flush` from a passive effect, `unmoved()` after an await, a macrotask) see the committed buffer. For discrete-event edits the passive effect was already flushed synchronously, which is why the harness cannot pin the move; for a non-discrete update (a timer, a continuous event) the move closes a window in which a landing save could read a stale key. App-shell tests run under happy-dom, where layout effects run at commit; React is 19.2.8 in dev with a `^18 || ^19` peer range, and only React 18 server rendering warns on a layout effect, which the Studio surface, a client editor, does not exercise.

**`doReorderFields` (right).** It writes `setObjDraft(body)` and takes `sendingObjDraft(body)`: the hook's snapshot is `objDraft`, so once the write commits the pending key equals the claim's key, and a field added during the flight moves it. It leaves `lastAttemptRef` alone, which is correct: the reorder never sets dirty, so the timer has nothing to dedupe against, and a later autosave key differs anyway. The pin and the control cover both branches.

**No NavTree row, no import line (right).** The import block is `:17` to `:139` and `NavTree` is `:1403` to `:1431`; the source hunks start at `:184` and then `:1687`, and none touches either. The diff adds no import: `DraftSend` and `draftSnapshotKey` are file-local.

**The two ablation legs (coherent; read as reported, not re-run).** Leg A (the claim always unmoved) 6 red / 6 green: the four in-flight pins here plus the two in-flight pins of objectui#11189's suite are exactly the pins the check carries; the Data control, the nav undo case (unmoved is the right answer there) and the four other objectui#11189 pins do not depend on it. Leg B (Automations' unconditional clear restored) 1 red / 11 green, the Automations pin alone. Both legs total 12, six here and six there. The first leg B attempt was a tool refusal before any run, not a reading. Restores blob-equal to the head.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11204-draft-autosave-in-flight-edit.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell` patch. Right: a behaviour fix in a module-private hook and its callers inside one file. `useDraftAutoSave` is not exported (`:217`), the three pillars' props are untouched, and no schema, type or accepted set moves. The text names the four editors and the nav undo change accurately. Changeset Declaration, Bump Policy, Claim Re-read, Fixed Group Check and Overwrite Report are green on the head. `Clause-②: no` — right, on the same ground.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. PR title "sent-snapshot check" against the order's "generation check": the direction said "snapshot or generation"; the title names the branch taken. Answered; not a deviation.
2. The detached base worktree and the uncommitted probe file: process only; the file list carries no probe file and the type-check listing the dev cites has none. Answered.
3. The hook's return shape and the layout-effect move: judged in ①, right.
4. `doReorderFields` inside the file surface: the card names Data's clears as a site and the claim names `DataPillar`'s hook caller; a second post-await clear in the same pillar is inside that surface, and it was measured before the fix. Answered.
5. Ablation leg B's refused first attempt: a no-op, re-run with a distinct replacement. Answered.
6. `open_questions`: none.
7. Out-of-scope 1 (a flow or page switch inside the debounce, while the load is slow, writes the old leaf's document to the newly opened leaf; Automations and the page inspector measured, Data read as safe). Class (a) at a public door on a writable package: a cross-item write, worse than the loss this card fixes, and its reach is every slow load. Verified not introduced and not touched here: the timer effect's dependencies are unchanged in effect (`api` is stable), the save is read through `saveRef` as on base, the load effects are untouched, and the layout-effect move changes nothing at the 1.5 s scale. Data is safe because `:3148` clears dirty synchronously before its await. It does not bear on this verdict. Escalated to the seat as the family closure card it names, with objectui#11203 as a member; the hook-level remedy the dev offers (drop a send whose target changed) fits the direction's "fix it once" better than a per-pillar clear.
8. Out-of-scope 2 (carrier objectui#11203). Yes, this PR opens one more interleaving to that card's spurious save: a nav save landing after a package switch has installed the other app now reads moved and leaves `navDirty` set, and the unblocked timer then saves the switched-to app; `navGen` cleared it because an install never bumped. It is not a regression this PR must close: the ordinary path (an unsaved edit, then a switch) already reaches the same save on `main` and is the wider window; the seat sequenced objectui#11203 immediately after this card for this very state; closing it here would mean an install-aware exception, a second mechanism of the kind the direction retired; and objectui#11203's reset of `navDirty` and `editNav` at the switch closes both, since the landing claim only declines to clear and never sets. Escalated: the seat's objectui#11203 dispatch must name this interleaving (a switch during an in-flight nav save) as a pin.
